items.title: Qatar shoots down two Iranian jets in Gulf first

featured_image.name: Qatar air force shoots down two aircraft from Iran: Defence ...

items.description:
Qatar's air force shot down two Iranian Sukhoi Su-24 fighter jets on Monday, marking the first time a Gulf country has engaged a manned Iranian aircraft since Tehran began its retaliatory bombardment of the region three days ago. The Qatari Defense Ministry said its forces also intercepted seven ballistic missiles and five drones, with all projectiles neutralized before reaching their intended targets.[1][2][3]

The shootdowns came on the third day of Iranian strikes across the Persian Gulf, launched in retaliation for joint US-Israeli attacks on Iran that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on February 28. Iran has targeted multiple Gulf states hosting US military assets, turning the skies over Doha, Dubai, Manama, and Kuwait City into active conflict zones.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: Trump says Iran war likely to last at least a month

featured_image.name: WATCH LIVE: Trump may address war with Iran at Medal of Honor ceremony

items.description:
President Trump used a Medal of Honor ceremony at the White House on Monday to deliver his first live public remarks on the U.S.-led military campaign against Iran, warning that operations could last four to five weeks and acknowledging that more American casualties are likely as the conflict enters its third day.[1][2]

The president spoke after awarding the Medal of Honor to three U.S. Army soldiers — Master Sergeant Roderick W. Edmonds, honored posthumously for protecting Jewish prisoners of war during World War II; Staff Sergeant Michael H. Ollis, honored posthumously for his heroism in Afghanistan; and Command Sergeant Major Terry P. Richardson, a retired Vietnam War veteran. The juxtaposition of honoring past military valor with the reality of a new armed conflict lent the ceremony an unusual gravity.[3][4]

items.title: Macron offers to station French nuclear weapons in Europe

featured_image.name: Reading between the lines of the new France-UK nuclear ...

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron declared on Monday that France will increase the size of its nuclear arsenal and strengthen its deterrence posture, warning that the world faces a growing risk of conflicts crossing the nuclear threshold. Speaking from the Île Longue submarine base in Brittany — home to France's four ballistic missile submarines — Macron described the current era as one of "geopolitical turmoil filled with dangers" and called for a "fortification" of France's deterrence.[1]

The address, closely watched by European allies, marks the most consequential shift in French nuclear doctrine in decades. Macron introduced a concept of "forward deterrence" and, for the first time, formally offered to station French nuclear weapons in other European nations, following a model long used by the United States, which maintains warheads in Germany, Belgium, Italy, and Turkey under NATO sharing arrangements.[2][3]

items.title: Trump pushes Venezuela model for Iran transition

featured_image.name: An Emboldened Trump Makes Big Bets in Venezuela, Iran and ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump said on March 1 that he envisions applying the political transition model used in Venezuela to post-Khamenei Iran, calling the Venezuelan operation "the perfect, the perfect scenario" in a phone interview with The New York Times.[1]

The remarks came days after U.S. and Israeli forces launched coordinated strikes against more than 1,000 sites across Iran on February 28, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and, according to Trump, eliminating much of Iran's military command. Trump announced Khamenei's death in a social media post hours after the operation began.[2][3]

items.title: Euro zone factory growth hits 44-month high as Germany returns to expansion

featured_image.name: Euro zone factory growth hit 44-month high in February, PMI ...

items.description: Euro zone manufacturing returned to growth territory in February for the first time since August, while UK factory activity expanded for a fourth straight month, according to purchasing managers' surveys released Monday. Meanwhile, India's industrial production growth fell sharply to 4.8% in January, down from a two-year high of 8% the previous month.

items.title: Lebanon bans Hezbollah military operations after Israeli strikes kill dozens

featured_image.name: IDF and Hezbollah battle in Lebanon after Iran missile attack

items.description:
Lebanon's government on Monday banned all of Hezbollah's military and security operations, demanding the Iran-backed group hand over its weapons to the state after the militia's rocket and drone attacks on Israel triggered devastating retaliatory airstrikes that killed at least 31 people across the country.[1][2]

Prime Minister Nawaf Salam announced the decision following an emergency cabinet session, declaring that "any military or security action carried out from Lebanese territory outside the legitimate institutions" is unlawful. He urged Hezbollah to surrender its arms and said the Lebanese army would immediately begin implementing its plan to disarm the group north of the Litani River.[2][1]

items.title: Study: Climate pledges would still overshoot Paris 2°C target

featured_image.name: Despite Some Progress, Countries' New Climate Plans Largely Fall ...

items.description:
Even if every nation fulfills its current climate commitments, the world is still on track to warm by roughly 2.5°C — nearly half a degree above the Paris Agreement's 2°C safety threshold — according to a peer-reviewed study published in the journal Environmental Science & Policy.[1][2]

The research, led by Assistant Professor Taeyoung Jin of Jeonbuk National University in collaboration with Pusan National University, modeled climate and economic outcomes through the year 2300 using the Regional Integrated Model of Climate and the Economy (RICE-2010). The study projects that under a net-zero scenario reflecting current national pledges, global temperatures would rise approximately 2.48°C by 2300. Under a business-as-usual scenario with no emission cuts, warming could reach as high as 7°C over the same period.[3][2][4][1]

items.title: Claude AI hit by worldwide outage across all platforms

featured_image.name: Is Claude Down? Outage Reports Briefly Spike For Anthropic's AI

items.description:
Anthropic's Claude AI chatbot went down on Monday in a worldwide outage that left users unable to access the platform across its web interface, mobile apps, and developer API.

The company flagged the incident on its status page at 11:49 UTC on March 2, 2026, posting an initial "Investigating" notice, followed by an update at 12:06 UTC stating the investigation was ongoing. Users attempting to reach the service reported failed requests, timeouts, and error messages including "This isn't working right now" and upstream connection termination errors.[1][2]

items.title: Three US F-15s shot down by Kuwaiti air defenses in friendly fire incident

featured_image.name: Several' US fighter jets crash over Kuwait, military ...

items.description:
Three US Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jets crashed in Kuwait on Monday morning after being mistakenly shot down by Kuwaiti air defenses during active combat operations against Iran, the US Central Command confirmed.

All six crew members ejected safely and are in stable condition after being recovered and transported to hospitals, CENTCOM said in a statement. The incident marks the first loss of American aircraft in the four-day-old conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran.[1]

items.title: India's factory growth hits 4-month high as UK, Australia slow

featured_image.name: India's bid to match China's factory power gets a reality ...

items.description: Manufacturing activity across major economies showed diverging trends in February 2026, with Australia and the United Kingdom losing steam even as India's factory sector accelerated to a four-month high, according to purchasing managers' index data released this week by S&P Global.

items.title: NOAA sees up to 60% chance El Nino forms later in 2026

featured_image.name: El Nino is brewing: Here's what it means for US weather in 2026

items.description:
The El Niño weather phenomenon could develop later this year, potentially pushing global temperatures to new record heights, according to the latest forecasts from U.S. and international climate agencies.

NOAA's Climate Prediction Center estimates a 50 to 60 percent chance that El Niño will form during the July-to-September period and beyond. The World Meteorological Organization is expected to issue an update on El Niño on Tuesday.[1][2]

items.title: Satellite images show smoke over Dubai as Iran's Gulf strikes enter third day

featured_image.name: Satellite images show smoke rising over Dubai after Iranian ...

items.description: Satellite imagery captured on March 1 has revealed thick plumes of black smoke rising over Dubai's skyline, offering stark visual evidence of the damage caused by Iran's ongoing retaliatory missile and drone attacks across the Persian Gulf region. The before-and-after images — comparing clear skies on February 24 with smoke columns and burn marks days later — underscore how quickly the conflict between the United States and Iran has reached the doorstep of the Gulf's most prominent commercial hub.[1][2]

items.title: AWS outage spreads to Bahrain as Gulf strikes continue

featured_image.name: Amazon's Cloud Service AWS Hit With Iranian Missile In UAE ...

items.description:
Amazon Web Services suffered a major disruption to its cloud infrastructure in the United Arab Emirates after unidentified objects struck one of its data centers on Sunday, sparking a fire that forced an extended power shutdown as Iranian retaliatory strikes battered the Gulf region.

AWS confirmed on its status page that at approximately 4:30 a.m. PST on March 1, its Availability Zone mec1-az2 in the ME-CENTRAL-1 Region "was impacted by objects that struck the data center, creating sparks and fire". The fire department cut power to the entire facility, including backup generators, while crews worked to extinguish the blaze. The company did not confirm or deny whether the incident was connected to the Iranian strikes when asked by Reuters.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Iran's top security chief rejects talks with US as strikes enter third day

featured_image.name: Ali Larijani appointed as secretary of Iran's Supreme ...

items.description:
Ali Larijani, the head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, declared on Monday that Tehran "will not negotiate with the United States," flatly rejecting claims that Iranian officials had sought to restart talks with Washington. The statement, posted on X, came hours after President Donald Trump told The Atlantic that Iran's new leadership wanted dialogue and that he had "agreed to talk".[1][2][3][4]

Larijani's rebuke marks a sharp public break with the diplomatic track Trump floated over the weekend, even as US and Israeli strikes on Iran entered their third day following the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Saturday.[5][6]

items.title: Israel strikes Beirut after Hezbollah shatters ceasefire with rocket attack

featured_image.name: Israel strikes Beirut for the first time since a ceasefire ...

items.description:
Israel launched its most intensive airstrikes on Beirut since the 2024 war early Monday, pounding Hezbollah-controlled southern suburbs of the Lebanese capital after the Iran-backed group fired rockets and drones at northern Israel for the first time since a U.S.-brokered ceasefire took effect in November 2024. More than a dozen explosions rocked Beirut beginning around 2:40 a.m. local time, sending residents fleeing on foot and by car and clogging roads out of the city.[1][2]

The exchange marks a dramatic widening of the conflict that erupted over the weekend when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.[3][4]

items.title: Iran fires missiles at Israel and US sites across Gulf in retaliation

featured_image.name: Israel strikes Beirut suburb targeting Hezbollah drone depot ...

items.description:
Iran launched a sweeping wave of missile and drone attacks against Israel and U.S. military installations across the Persian Gulf over the weekend, striking targets in at least eight countries in retaliation for a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Saturday.

The Iranian offensive, which began hours after coordinated American and Israeli strikes hit Tehran and other Iranian cities on February 28, has killed at least nine Israelis in a single ballistic missile strike on Beit Shemesh, three U.S. service members, and several others across the Gulf region, while injuring hundreds and paralyzing air travel across the Middle East.

items.title: Factory growth accelerates across Indonesia, India, Thailand in February

featured_image.name: Indonesia's manufacturing activity hits 11-month high ahead ...

items.description: Factory activity across three of Southeast and South Asia's largest economies gained momentum in February, with purchasing managers' index data released Monday by S&P Global showing accelerating expansion in Indonesia, India, and Thailand, driven by strengthening domestic demand and rising new orders.

items.title: Melania Trump to chair UN Security Council amid US war on Iran

featured_image.name: Melania Trump set to make history at UN Security Council meeting

items.description:
First Lady Melania Trump is scheduled to preside over a United Nations Security Council meeting on Monday afternoon, an unprecedented appearance that was planned weeks ago but now collides with the reality of active US military operations in Iran.

The session, titled "Children, Technology, and Education in Conflict," will mark the first time a sitting US First Lady has chaired the 15-member council, according to UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric. The meeting comes as the United States assumes the rotating presidency of the Security Council for March.[1][2][3]

items.title: BOJ deputy governor says rate hikes to continue

featured_image.name: Bank of Japan deputy governor says rate hikes likely to ...

items.description:
Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino said Monday that the central bank should continue raising interest rates as it moves toward a more neutral monetary policy, reinforcing expectations that further tightening lies ahead even as the Japanese economy sends mixed signals.

"While the Bank's policy remains somewhat accommodative, it should gradually shift to a more neutral stance through moderate policy rate hikes," Himino said in a speech to local business leaders in Wakayama.[1][2]

items.title: Canada's Carney arrives in Delhi for Modi talks amid Iran crisis

featured_image.name: PM Carney lands in New Delhi, plans to meet Modi tomorrow

items.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney landed in New Delhi on Saturday as part of a three-nation tour aimed at deepening trade ties with Indo-Pacific partners, even as U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran and Tehran's retaliatory attacks across the Middle East cast a shadow over global diplomacy.
